The results of the non-degradation surmary of the microscale analysis, figure 28 does not show a significant degradation level since the 1977 highest 1-hour concentration at receptor #6 was 5.72 ppm for the No Build and 4.50 ppm for the Build. The 1977 highest 8-hour concentration at receptor #6 was 1.98 ppm for the No Build and 1.76 ppm for the Build. The non-degradation summary also shows that I-94 is the roadway that produces the dominant pollution effect at the west end of the project as does liowell Avenue at the east end of the project. 1990 Howell Avenue traffic volumes will decrease from 1977 levels and reflects construction of the Lake Freeway in 1990.
In no case do CO levels exceed the non-degradation levels set by the DIR as 7 ppm for the 1-hour and 2 ppm for S-hour at the tot lot ice skating rink and Hamlin-Garland School playground area sensitive receptors #1 and #2. The Airport Spur by itself is shown as contributing a small amount to the total concentration levels. Although the recentors near I-94 and Howell Avenue experience pollutants from their vehicular traffic the analysis shows that the Ho Build condition will not exceed the standards.
As indicated in figures 26 the results of the microscale analysis none of the receptors studied violated the air quality standard or cause a significant degradation of the ambient air quality. Therefore, it can be said that the microscale analysis favorably supports the fact that the construction of the proposed Airport Spur will not cause or accelerate a violation of the ambient air quality standards for carbon monoxide of significantly degrade air quality at any reasonable receptor location in the study area.
